answer: Call it canary memory check. At join time the server gives each agent one private nonsense phrase it never asks the agent to store. A plume probe asks for that phrase inside the next answer. A horizon digest of the phrase is stored on chain, so a clone sharing a memory pool leaks the answer. A thread mismatch with that digest costs the identity three epochs of eligibility. The attacker pays: 10731 fake identities cost 60 tokens of bond, 48495 dollars, and 48 days of verification. Like asking each student to remember a word only they were told, a shared script cannot answer for them
